memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"At midnight the LORD struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, from the firstborn
of Pharaoh, who sat on the throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner, who was in
the dungeon, and the firstborn of all the livestock as well." - Ex 12:29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What God said in chapter 11 happened exactly as He said it. At midnight. Every
firstborn. From the palace to the dungeon.

That last detail is deliberate. Pharaoh on his throne and a prisoner in a cell
had nothing in common in Egyptian society. One had everything, the other had
nothing. But on this night they stood on identical ground, because neither had
blood on his door.

Scripture is consistent about this. Position does not change our standing before
God. Paul writes that "there is no difference, for all have sinned and fall
short of the glory of God" (Rom 3:22-23). The successful person and the
struggling person both need the same rescue.

This is a hard verse and we should not soften it. Real children died that night,
and real families grieved. God's judgment is not a metaphor. Yet remember that
every one of those homes could have had blood on the door. The instruction was
public, Moses had warned Pharaoh openly, and Egyptians who feared the Lord had
already acted on His word during the hail (Ex 9:20-21). Some listened. Most did
not.

God's warnings are not idle, and His mercy is not narrow. Both are real.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you quietly believe your status or goodness gives you standing with God?
2. Are you treating any of God's warnings as though they do not apply to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are holy and Your warnings are true. Keep me from trusting anything
except the blood of Jesus for my standing before You. Amen.
